title: Intelligent Router for LLM Workloads: Improving Performance Through Workload-Aware Load Balancing
technique: Heuristic-guided RL router across LLM instances using a trainable response-length predictor and a prefill/decode workload-mixing impact estimator in the reward

optimized_metrics.evidence: Our goal is to minimize end-to-end latency by assigning requests to LLM instances

reward formulation: a) a negative penalty for requests in the queue, decreasing as requests are processed ... b) a positive reward for each completed request, and c) a workload impact estimator-based penalty

headline_claim.text: achieves over 11% lower end-to-end latency than existing approaches on a mix of public datasets and 7.8% lower end-to-end latency on real workload data with diverse input and output trends from Cloud Provider X

reported_metrics.where: Fig 5a average TBT; Fig 6c TBT distribution
Fig 5c queue length at router and model instances

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we report the end-to-end latency, Time-To-First-Token (TTFT), which is the time taken for the user to see the initial response, and Time-Between-Tokens (TBT), which is the average token streaming latency (Patel et al., 2023). Additionally, we report the throughput achieved by different approaches.
metric_definitions.notes: TBT defined as the average token streaming latency (a per-request-average, TPOT-like) while Fig 6c shows a TBT distribution; TTFT = time until user sees initial response (queueing at router/instance implicit); throughput reported as prompt and generation throughput, units not defined

load_regime: fixed average arrival rate (lambda = 20 req/s, requests sampled uniformly at random from dataset), 4 instances; real workload trace from Cloud Provider X
tradeoff_acknowledged: Round Robin initially has better average TBT than RL early on, but TBT grows over time as more requests accumulate; workload-guided penalties keep prompt/generation throughput similar to RR (no throughput gain claimed)
hardware: 4x V100 (main), A100 with Llama-3.1-8B (generalization); simulator/profiles for Llama-2-7b on V100
workloads: mix of public datasets (§4) and real workloads from Cloud Provider X
extractor_notes: objective is mean end-to-end latency only (no tail percentile). E2E here is request completion latency including queueing at router/instance. Improvements are modest (11.06% table; 7.8% real trace) and classical heuristics (JSQ, max-capacity, min-min) beat RR by only 0.46-2.6%. The abstract states the scheduler can 'serve as a standard for benchmarking'. No SLO.
load_class_quote: 'fixed average arrival rate (lambda = 20 req/s, requests sampled uniformly at random from dataset)' on 4 instances; real workload trace from Cloud Provider X
